summary.verdict: H0 (no usable physics floor for POTENCY-RANKING on thrombin): docking ranks potency among thrombin BINDERS no better than random (overall AUROC 0.4285, slightly anti-predictive). This is expected and honest — MoleculeACE compounds are a CONGENERIC BINDER SERIES, and docking is known to be poor at FINE potency-ranking (its hardest case), which is DISTINCT from coarse active-vs-decoy hit-finding where C1 saw a weak-but-real signal (Mpro AUROC 0.63). The novel-chemotype physics test is UNDERPOWERED (only 5 novel actives — thrombin data is analog-heavy), so 'physics beats similarity on novel' (0.5226 vs 0.0912) is BOTH tautological (novel:=low-similarity rigs similarity to fail) AND noise. Consensus (physics+similarity) 0.6958 < ligand-similarity alone (~0.84, HIT1) — adding docking HURTS. NET molecule-half map: ligand methods are analog-bound (HIT1); docking is weak-but-real for active-vs-decoy (C1) but USELESS for within-series potency-ranking (HIT2); no method has strong traction on genuinely novel chemotypes — the information ceiling. SCOPE: single favourable target, Vina, potency data (not decoys), 5 novel actives, 24 failed docks, not wet-lab.
